edges.notes: musl provides syscall wrappers and POSIX/C API on Linux userland ABIs.
musl shared objects and ld-musl participate in ELF dynamic linking on musl-based Linux systems.
musl implements the C standard library for hosted C environments on musl Linux triplets.
GCC is commonly used to build musl-based systems (e.g. Alpine Linux toolchains).
GNU ld links musl objects and shared libraries in typical musl GNU/Linux flows.
Clang can target musl environments when using appropriate triplets and sysroots.
GDB can debug musl-linked executables similarly to glibc-linked programs on Linux.
LLDB may be used on musl-based Linux systems for C/C++ debugging (environment-dependent).
musl supports Linux ports on multiple architectures documented in the project, including RISC-V.
Many popular OCI images use Alpine or other musl-based bases, pulled and run via Docker.

libc++abi can be layered on musl in Clang libc++ sysroots when packaging matches.
Alpine Linux uses musl as its standard C library on supported architectures per Alpine documentation.
